h: Outlet shopping, classic cars and a Cotswolds edge
p: Bicester is best known for one thing: Bicester Village, the designer outlet that draws shoppers from all over the world. If half the family wants a browse and the other half would rather do anything else, a trampoline session is the perfect peace treaty. Drop the jumpers off, grab a coffee or a bargain, and meet back up once everyone's worn out. Bicester has two railway stations, Bicester Village and Bicester North, with trains towards Oxford, London and Birmingham, which makes it easy to visit without the car.

Petrolheads should head to Bicester Motion, on the site of the former RAF Bicester airfield. It's home to classic car specialists, historic buildings and regular events, and wandering around the old airfield buildings is fascinating even if you don't know your carburettor from your crankshaft. Check what's on before you go, as event days can be busy.

For a full day out, Oxford is a short drive or train ride away, with its colleges, museums and riverside walks. The Pitt Rivers Museum and the Oxford University Museum of Natural History share a building and are free to enter, with dinosaurs downstairs and a treasure trove of curiosities next door. Blenheim Palace in Woodstock, birthplace of Winston Churchill, is also within easy reach, with huge parkland, a maze and seasonal events. Back in Bicester itself, Market Square and Sheep Street have independent shops and cafes for a quick refuel. A practical tip: traffic around the outlet can be heavy at weekends and in the run-up to Christmas, so allow extra time if your session is booked for a busy Saturday.
